title: Lincoln’s Gettysburg Address and Second Inaugural
author: Abraham Lincoln
openingText: Four score and seven years ago, our fathers brought forth upon this continent a new nation: conceived in liberty, and dedicated to the proposition that all men are created equal.
about:
On November 19, 1863, four and a half months after the battle, Abraham Lincoln spoke at the dedication of a cemetery for Union soldiers at Gettysburg, Pennsylvania. His address is only a few paragraphs long. On March 4, 1865, as the war was ending, he gave his second inaugural address, a longer speech that looks back on the cause of the war and ahead to what comes after it.

This package puts the two speeches side by side as two reading units. The English baseline is the text distributed by Project Gutenberg. The speeches are short enough to read in one sitting and then again slowly.

whyItMatters.title: A speech that fits on a page
whyItMatters.body: The Gettysburg Address uses a few hundred words to say what the war is for and what the living owe the dead. Its sentences are short and built on repeated phrases, so each one can be read aloud. Reading it slowly shows how much work each word does.

whyItMatters.title: A president looks at the war’s cause
whyItMatters.body: In the Second Inaugural, Lincoln names slavery as the cause of the war and asks what the suffering of both sides means. He does not claim victory in the speech. Instead he speaks of charity and of binding up the nation’s wounds. The tone is easy to compare with how politicians speak after a win today.

whyItMatters.title: Two speeches, two moods
whyItMatters.body: The first is a dedication at a graveyard and the second an inauguration at the end of a long war. Read together they show Lincoln moving from remembering the dead to planning for peace. The pairing is useful because the speeches are so different in length.

angleCards.title: Count the repetitions
angleCards.text: Notice which words and phrases return in the Gettysburg Address and what each repetition adds.
angleCards.angleObjective: I’m reading Lincoln’s two speeches to see how repeated words and phrases build meaning in a very short text.

angleCards.title: Follow the argument about the war
angleCards.text: Track how the Second Inaugural explains what the war is about and who is responsible.
angleCards.angleObjective: I’m reading Lincoln’s two speeches to understand how he explains the cause and meaning of the Civil War.

angleCards.title: Compare the two speeches
angleCards.text: Set the dedication at the cemetery beside the inauguration and compare their tone, length and audience.
angleCards.angleObjective: I’m reading Lincoln’s two speeches to compare how he speaks to mourners and how he speaks to a nation at war’s end.

angleCards.title: Read it aloud
angleCards.text: Read each speech aloud once, then listen for where the rhythm slows or lifts.
angleCards.angleObjective: I’m reading Lincoln’s two speeches to listen to their rhythm and how it carries the meaning.
